rationale.text: The test asks that all the text of the page can be enlarged to 200% by any one of three means: the browser's text enlargement, the browser's graphic zoom, or a component of the site. It exempts burned-in captions, text in images and text in a canvas. axe's meta-viewport faults a viewport meta element that sets user-scalable=no or a maximum-scale below 2. That blocks pinch zoom in some mobile browsers, which bears on the graphic zoom route only. It does not stop the browser's text enlargement, desktop zoom ignores it, and some mobile browsers override it, so the text may still be enlarged by another route or even by graphic zoom. The link is evidence only and partial: it looks at one element, not at the text. A custom check could find text that does not grow under zoom, such as a font size set only in viewport units, but a fault could prove failure only if all three routes failed, and the site component route needs judgment to find and interaction to use. Whether some text is exempt as text in an image is judgment as well. So the entry is none. Applicability is judgment: a page whose only text is exempt would be outside the test, which code cannot tell for certain. Needs lists state, because the third means is a component the user operates. Rendering the page with enlarged text or zoom is not one of the listed prerequisites.
